big_story.headline: Shielding Banking from Cyber Threats
big_story.subhead: PM MODI INAUGURATES RBI DATA CENTRE AND CYBERSECURITY INSTITUTE IN BHUBANESWAR
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The launch highlights a fresh strategic focus on protecting India's vital financial infrastructure from digital threats. Speaking at the inauguration, PM Modi warned against economic warfare and stressed the imperative need to shield the country's banking system from cyber terrorism.

The setup of these dedicated facilities reflects a modern priority for India as digital transaction volumes surge nationwide. By establishing localized security infrastructure, the central bank aims to strengthen defensive capabilities across critical payment channels. The Bhubaneswar center will also focus on specialized training to equip banking professionals with skills to neutralize cyber risks.

As global financial networks face increasingly complex digital attacks, India's proactive investment in cybersecurity signals a commitment to institutional resilience. Observers point out that building robust defenses is crucial to maintaining consumer confidence and economic stability. Financial institutions will now look to leverage the training and protocols established by the new RBI institute.
big_story.pullbox: Protecting digital financial networks against cyber warfare has become central to national security and banking stability in India.

explains.title: What is Financial Cybersecurity?
paragraphs: Financial cybersecurity encompasses the technologies, policies, and operational controls designed to protect banking systems, payment networks, and sensitive data from digital attacks.
In practice, central banks establish dedicated data centers, encryption standards, and threat monitoring facilities to safeguard financial infrastructure from cyber terrorism and fraudulent breaches.

Y Combinator-backed startup Firstwork has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Earlybird Venture Capital. This latest injection brings the company's total funding raised to $20 million as it continues its expansion.

The investment comes as early-stage tech platforms draw targeted capital commitments from prominent venture firms. With backing from Earlybird Venture Capital and Y Combinator, Firstwork plans to deploy the new funds to accelerate product innovation and scale its operational footprint.

story_1.headline: India and EU Target December Seal for Landmark FTA
paragraphs: India and the European Union are pushing to finalize their landmark Free Trade Agreement by December 2026. Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that negotiations are on track for a year-end seal, setting up an operational rollout in the first quarter of next year.

The deal is expected to be signed during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's scheduled visit to Brussels in December. Port and trade authorities across Europe have expressed high expectations for boosted bilateral exchange following the pact.

story_2.headline: FPIs Pull Out ₹48,056 Crore from Indian Equities
paragraphs: Foreign Portfolio Investors have pulled out ₹48,056 crore from Indian equities in October, driven by persistent global risk aversion. High international crude oil prices, ongoing Middle East tensions, and rising US Treasury yields have triggered significant foreign capital flight.

The massive monthly withdrawal marks one of the heaviest foreign sell-offs this year. Market participants continue to closely monitor US Federal Reserve policy expectations and global commodity trends for hints of stability.

story_3.headline: Piramal Finance Gains ₹3,000 Cr from DHFL Assets
paragraphs: Five years after acquiring Dewan Housing Finance Limited, Piramal Finance has gained ₹3,000 crore from stressed loans. The gain highlights steady recovery progress in resolving legacy non-performing assets taken over during the buyout.

geopolitics.headline: India and US Near Interim Trade Deal as Trump Policy Looms
paragraphs: India and the US are close to reaching a trade deal, according to US President Donald Trump. Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and the US Trade Representative recently held discussions on an early conclusion to an interim trade deal. Bilateral relations are moving toward deal-making as both sides work to lock in trade terms.

However, wider geopolitical issues such as Trump's looming policy on Iran add complexity to the negotiations. Indian businesses and exporters are tracking the talks closely to gauge market access and strategic alignment. A successful interim pact could provide much-needed policy certainty for cross-border trade.

big_story.headline: Market Sell-Off: Sensex Drops 400 Points, Infosys Down 3%
big_story.text: Indian stock markets opened sharply lower on Monday as the Sensex dropped 400 points and the Nifty fell below 22,500. Technology giant Infosys led the decline, sliding 3 percent in early trade. The drop reflects cautious sentiment across domestic equities as broader valuation pressures weigh on Indian stock benchmarks.

big_story.headline: ED Attaches ₹43.65 Crore in Electrotherm Bank Fraud Probe
big_story.text: The Enforcement Directorate attached assets worth ₹43.65 crore linked to Electrotherm as part of an investigation into an old ₹81.97-crore bank-fraud trail. Regulatory authorities continue to tighten action around historic financial default cases. For Indian banking oversight, it underscores persistent legal scrutiny against corporate fraud.

venture_vault.headline: Indian Startup Funding Drops 22% to ₹1,747 Crore Driven by AI Shift
venture_vault.text: Weekly startup funding in India fell 22 percent to ₹1,747 crore, even as artificial intelligence ventures captured half of the overall capital deployed. The investment concentration highlights a sharp pivot by venture capital toward deeptech platforms. For India's ecosystem, it shows how AI demand is restructuring startup financing.

venture_vault.headline: Blacksmith Hits Unicorn Status with $66 Million Funding Round
venture_vault.text: AI code testing platform Blacksmith raised $66 million in fresh capital, reaching a $1 billion valuation to achieve unicorn status. The round underscores rapid market demand for automated software infrastructure tools. The successful raise highlights global investor confidence in developer-focused artificial intelligence startups.

geopolitics.headline: Rotterdam Port Chief Sets High Hopes on India-EU Free Trade Deal
geopolitics.text: The chief of the Port of Rotterdam expressed very high expectations regarding the proposed India-EU Free Trade Agreement. Trade talks aim to deepen commercial shipping links and lower barriers between European markets and India. A finalised pact could significantly boost bilateral supply chain integration and port infrastructure investment.

geopolitics.headline: Tensions in West Asia and Rising Crude Prices Pressure Markets
geopolitics.text: Escalating conflict in West Asia combined with rising crude oil prices threatens to put sustained pressure on Indian financial markets. Higher global energy costs pose risks to India's import bill, currency stability, and inflation trajectory. The geopolitical stress highlights India's ongoing vulnerability to imported commodity shocks.
